newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on ample market liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on ample market liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 40 basis points to 18.25 percent in early trade on Thursday as liquidity pressures eased after the central bank's cutoff date had passed, traders said.
"Yesterday saw the cutoff date and everything began over again today. The market is usually a bit calmer after the cutoff," a trader said.
Wednesday was cutoff date for banks settling balances outstanding on checking accounts held with Banco de Mexico.

Dealers said liquidity pressures had also relaxed due to Banco de Mexico announcing it would now allow banks to have equal short and long positions in their final balance after each day's trading. Previously, banks were allowed to close each day with short positions equivalent to three times long positions held.
Fixed-income analysts said the new measure aimed to anchor secondary rates close to 19 percent.
"They are allowing a little more room for dealers to play with, especially for smaller banks because so far the big players have used the mechanism to push the market around," an analyst said.
"Now there will be broader-based participation and that will help stabilise rates," he added.
Overnight rates on bank paper had, meanwhile, fallen 20 basis points to 19.35 percent.

Traders said cautious optimism over the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting also reduced upside pressure on domestic secondary market rates. U.S. data released on Thursday were strong, but on the whole data released so far this week did not indicate the U.S. economy was overheating.

"The outlook is overwhelmingly favorable. Some do not expect Tuesday's FOMC meeting to raise rates at all and a 25 basis-point hike is within market forecasts, so that will not lead to much speculation," a trader said.

Total liquidity of 147 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank intervention. Traders said the central bank auctioned 40 million pesos late on Wednesday in order to help banks meet the cutoff date. participation.
